nodes.description: The initiating lesion is biallelic loss-of-function of CSTB. In most patients an unstable expansion of a dodecamer (12-mer) repeat in the CSTB promoter reduces transcription; a minority carry loss-of-function point/indel variants (e.g., a splice-site or nonsense variant), frequently in compound heterozygosity with the repeat expansion. The shared consequence is markedly reduced cystatin B, an intracellular thiol (cysteine) protease inhibitor.
nodes.id: CSTB Dodecamer Repeat Expansion and Cystatin B Deficiency

evidence.reference_title: Dodecamer repeat expansion in cystatin B gene in progressive myoclonus epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: the majority of EPM1 alleles contain expansions of a dodecamer (12-mer) repeat located about 70 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site

evidence.reference_title: Dodecamer repeat expansion in cystatin B gene in progressive myoclonus epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Normal alleles contain 2 or 3 copies of this repeat whereas mutant alleles contain more than 60 such repeats and have reduced levels of CSTB messenger RNA in blood but not in cell lines.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding cystatin B in progressive myoclonus epilepsy (EPM1).
evidence.snippet: Two mutations, a 3' splice site mutation and a stop codon mutation, were identified in the gene encoding cystatin B in EPM1 patients

evidence.reference_title: The Roles of Cystatin B in the Brain and Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 1.
evidence.snippet: The CSTB protein functions as an intracellular thiol protease inhibitor and inhibits Cathepsin function.

nodes.description: Loss of cortical GABAergic inhibition shifts the cortical excitation-inhibition balance toward excitation, producing latent network hyperexcitability. This manifests as the hallmark stimulus-sensitive (action- and reflex-activated) myoclonus and as generalized, including photosensitive, seizures.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of cortical GABA terminals in Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: loss of cortical GABA input occurs in a relevant animal model and in a case of human ULD, leading to a condition of latent hyperexcitability that favors myoclonus and seizures.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 1.
evidence.snippet: the myoclonic jerks are progressive, action activated, and treatment resistant, and can be severely disabling.

nodes.description: Dysarthria develops as part of the delayed cerebellar syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: Some years after the onset ataxia, incoordination, intentional tremor, and dysarthria develop.

nodes.description: Generalized tonic-clonic epileptic seizures, present from onset; these are generally well controlled by antiseizure medication, in contrast to the treatment-resistant myoclonus.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: characterized by age of onset from 6 to 16 years, stimulus-sensitive myoclonus, and tonic-clonic epileptic seizures.

nodes.description: Intention (intentional) tremor is a component of the cerebellar syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: Some years after the onset ataxia, incoordination, intentional tremor, and dysarthria develop.

nodes.description: Cystatin B deficiency removes physiological restraint on lysosomal cysteine cathepsins and, in parallel, impairs neuronal defenses against oxidative stress. Cystatin B is normally induced by oxidative stress and protects neurons; its loss produces impaired redox homeostasis, with the oxidative vulnerability shown to be mediated by the lysosomal protease cathepsin B.
nodes.id: Loss of Cathepsin Inhibition and Redox Imbalance

evidence.reference_title: Cystatin B deficiency sensitizes neurons to oxidative stress in progressive myoclonus epilepsy, EPM1.
evidence.snippet: The Cystatin B deficiency-induced predisposition to oxidative stress in neurons is mediated by the lysosomal protease Cathepsin B.

evidence.reference_title: Cystatin B deficiency sensitizes neurons to oxidative stress in progressive myoclonus epilepsy, EPM1.
evidence.snippet: increased lipid peroxidation, in the cerebellum of Cystatin B knock-out mice in vivo.

evidence.reference_title: The Roles of Cystatin B in the Brain and Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 1.
evidence.snippet: protection against oxidative stress, likely through regulation of mitochondrial function.

nodes.description: Patients remain largely mentally alert but show a mild decline in intellectual performance over time; formal neuropsychological assessment of large cohorts documents impaired cognitive performance relative to controls. This relative preservation of cognition distinguishes EPM1 from more severe progressive myoclonus epilepsies such as Lafora disease.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with EPM1 are mentally alert but show emotional lability, depression, and mild decline in intellectual performance over time.

evidence.reference_title: Cognitive functioning in progressive myoclonus epilepsy type 1 (Unverricht-Lundborg Disease, EPM1).
evidence.snippet: The cognitive performance of the EPM1 patient group was impaired.

nodes.description: The coupled cathepsin/redox derangement drives progressive neuronal apoptosis. In the cystatin B-null mouse the principal cytopathology is apoptotic loss of cerebellar granule neurons, and there is a preferential depletion of cortical GABAergic (inhibitory) interneurons, confirmed in human ULD cortex. This is the central effector that connects the molecular lesion to the myoclonus/seizure and cerebellar clinical arms.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive ataxia, myoclonic epilepsy and cerebellar apoptosis in cystatin B-deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: The principal cytopathology appears to be a loss of cerebellar granule cells, which frequently display condensed nuclei, fragmented DNA and other cellular changes characteristic of apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive ataxia, myoclonic epilepsy and cerebellar apoptosis in cystatin B-deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: cystatin B, a non-caspase cysteine protease inhibitor, has a role in preventing cerebellar apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of cortical GABA terminals in Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: In CSTB knockout mice, a progressive decrease in neocortex thickness was found, associated with a prevalent loss of GABA interneurons.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of cortical GABA terminals in Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: A marked reduction in VGAT labeling was found in the cortex of both CSTB knockout mice and an ULD patient.

nodes.description: Photosensitivity is characteristic, with photic stimulation triggering myoclonus and seizures (photoparoxysmal response).

evidence.reference_title: The Roles of Cystatin B in the Brain and Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 1.
evidence.snippet: EPM1 patients suffer from photo-sensitive seizures, stimulus-sensitive myoclonus, nocturnal myoclonic seizures, ataxia and dysarthria.

nodes.description: Cerebellar ataxia and incoordination develop some years after seizure onset and progress over time, reflecting cerebellar neurodegeneration.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: Some years after the onset ataxia, incoordination, intentional tremor, and dysarthria develop.

evidence.reference_title: Dodecamer repeat expansion in cystatin B gene in progressive myoclonus epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: onset between 6 and 13 years followed by variable progression to mental deterioration and cerebellar ataxia.

nodes.description: Progressive apoptotic loss of cerebellar neurons, together with the cognitive consequences of diffuse neurodegeneration, produces the delayed and slowly progressive clinical arm of EPM1: cerebellar ataxia, incoordination, intention tremor, and dysarthria, with a mild decline in cognition over time while patients remain largely mentally alert.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive ataxia, myoclonic epilepsy and cerebellar apoptosis in cystatin B-deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: mice lacking cystatin B develop myoclonic seizures and ataxia, similar to symptoms seen in the human disease.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: Some years after the onset ataxia, incoordination, intentional tremor, and dysarthria develop.

nodes.description: The clinical hallmark: stimulus-sensitive, action- and reflex-activated myoclonus that is progressive and treatment resistant, and can be severely disabling.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical picture of EPM1-Unverricht-Lundborg disease.
evidence.snippet: characterized by age of onset from 6 to 16 years, stimulus-sensitive myoclonus, and tonic-clonic epileptic seizures.
